disposition.title: Nevo's Colin de Verdière stress-freeness conjecture

literal_record.title: Nevo's Colin de Verdière stress-freeness conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $\mu(G)$ denote the Colin de Verdière parameter of $G$. A graph is **generically $k$-stress free** if it has no nonzero generic $k$-stress. **Nevo's conjecture.** If

$$
\mu(G)\leq k,
$$

then $G$ is generically $k$-stress free. This conjecture is proved in the source for $k=5$ and $k=6$, while the source gives no resolution for the general statement.
literal_record.source_name: Boris Albar and Daniel Gonçalves, “On triangles in K_r-minor free graphs”, arXiv:1304.5468 (2013).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5468

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2013). “This conjecture has been proved for $k \leq 5$ but remains open for $k \geq 6$.”

disposition.title: Double-Critical Hadwiger Conjecture
disposition.statement: A connected graph is **double-critical $k$-chromatic** if it has chromatic number $k$ and, for every edge $uv$, deleting $u$ and $v$ lowers the chromatic number by $2$. **Double-Critical Hadwiger Conjecture.** Every double-critical $k$-chromatic graph contains a $K_k$ minor. The conjecture is proved by the cited authors for $k\leq 7$, while the case $k=8$ is open in the source.

**Grinshpun–Sárközy powers-of-cycles conjecture.** The vertex set of every $2$-colored complete graph can be covered by at most

disposition.title: The graphic Merino–Welsh conjectures
disposition.literal:
Let $G$ be a graph with no bridges and no loops. Let $\tau(G)$ be its number of spanning trees, let $(G)$ be its number of acyclic orientations, and let $^*(G)$ be its number of totally cyclic orientations. **Graphic Merino–Welsh conjectures.** The following inequalities hold:

$$
\max\left((G),^*(G)\right)\geq\tau(G),
$$

$$
(G)+^*(G)\geq 2\cdot\tau(G),
$$

and

$$
(G)\cdot^*(G)\geq\tau(G)^2.
$$

The third, multiplicative, inequality is the strongest and implies the additive inequality, which in turn implies the first. The conjectures have been proved for several graph families, including wheels, complete graphs, and series-parallel graphs, but remain open in general.

disposition.title: Sink-independence conjecture for recurrent-configuration class sums

literal.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be a strongly connected digraph and let $s$ be a vertex of $G$. Write $G_{\backslash s^{+}}$ for the digraph obtained by removing all outgoing arcs of $s$, so that $s$ is a global sink. Fix an order $v_1\prec v_2\prec\cdots\prec v_{n-1}$ on the vertices distinct from $s$, where $n=|V|$, and define $r_i\in\mathbb{Z}^{n-1}$ by $r_{i,j}=\deg_G(v_i,v_j)$ for $i\ne j$ and $r_{i,i}=\deg_G^+(v_i)$. Set $\beta_i=\deg_G(s,v_i)$, let $\mathcal{C}$ be the recurrent configurations of $G_{\backslash s^{+}}$, and define $c_1\sim c_2$ when $c_1-c_2$ lies in the subgroup $\langle r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_{n-1},\beta\rangle$ of $(\mathbb{Z}^{n-1},+)$. For $B\in\mathcal{C}/\!\sim$, let

$$
\textbf{\texttt{sum}}\,_{G,s}(B)=\max\left\{\deg_G^+(s)+\sum_{v\ne s}c(v):c\in B\right\}.
$$

**Sink-independence conjecture.** The sequence $\left(\textbf{\texttt{sum}}\,_{G,s}(B)\right)_{B\in\mathcal{C}/\sim}$ is independent of the choice of $s$, up to a permutation of its entries. If $G$ is Eulerian, then $\beta\in\langle r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}\rangle$, so the equivalence relation simplifies accordingly. If true, this would generalize the specialization $T_G(1,y)$ of the Tutte polynomial from undirected graphs to strongly connected digraphs.

disposition.title: The near-bipartite characterization conjecture for ${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect graphs

literal.statement: For a graph $G$, let $\operatorname{STAB}(G)$ be its stable set polytope, $\operatorname{NB}(G)$ the near-bipartite polyhedral relaxation, and ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ the Lovász–Schrijver positive semidefinite relaxation. A polyhedron is **polyhedral** if it can be described by finitely many linear inequalities. **The near-bipartite characterization conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the following four statements are equivalent: (1) $\operatorname{STAB}(G)=\operatorname{NB}(G)$; (2) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{STAB}(G)$; (3) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{NB}(G)$; and (4) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ is polyhedral. This would characterize the graphs on which the Lovász–Schrijver operator reaches the stable set polytope using the near-bipartite relaxation; the paper presents it as an open conjecture.
